name: マーガレット スプーン (Marguerite Spoon)

claims.text: スコーンはすべて小麦粉使用の厨房で製造。専用グルテンフリー設備や交差汚染対策についての記述は確認されていない。
全製品に乳製品（発酵バター・生クリーム）が使用されており、ヴィーガン向け製品との分離製造は行われていないとみられる。
アレルギー対応や食物制限に関するスタッフ対応についての情報は公式・ブログ・レビューいずれにも見当たらない。来店前にInstagram DMで問い合わせることが推奨される（電話注文不可）。
米粉を使ったグルテンフリーのカヌレ（外はカリッと、中はふわふわ）が少なくとも一時期提供されていたことが確認されている。
No allergen menu, dedicated GF prep area, or cross-contamination protocols were found across Tabelog, HotPepper, or any review sources.

Standard wheat-containing soy sauce is integral to Japanese kaiseki and sushi — used in dipping sauce, shari seasoning, and course marinades. No wheat-free soy sauce alternative (tamari/GF shoyu) is documented for this restaurant.
Bonito (katsuo) dashi is a core building block of the menu per diner reviews; all courses likely contain fish-based stock unless a special accommodation is arranged in advance.

No documented allergy-handling protocol or staff allergy training was found. The restaurant's online reservation notes ask guests to avoid strong fragrances, but no dietary restriction pre-screening process is mentioned.
Dashi base is made from natural kombu and bonito — kombu portions are inherently gluten-free and iodine-rich; advance notice to the kitchen may allow adjustment of fish-stock components.
No information available on cross-contamination controls. The kitchen handles wheat-based soy sauce throughout all cooking.

The signature tare (glaze) used on all eel dishes is wheat-based soy sauce that has been continuously replenished since 1848. Wheat soy sauce is inherent to the product; no tamari or GF alternative is documented.
All dishes are animal-based (eel, oyster, fish dashi). There is no plant-based cooking track and therefore unavoidable animal cross-contact throughout.
No allergy handling protocols or allergen menus are documented on any source including the official website, Tabelog, or Gnavi listings.

name: おばんざいと地酒 ゆう菜 (Obanzai to Jizake Yusai)

claims.text: 春巻きなど小麦粉使用メニューが通常ラインナップに含まれており、調理場での交差汚染リスクを排除できない。
和食・おばんざいの調理では一般的な醤油（小麦含有）が使用されると考えられる。グルテンフリー醤油使用の明示はない。
かつお出汁・魚介・鶏肉を使うメニューが同じ厨房で調理される。植物性のみへの対応について明記なし。
オーナーが管理栄養士の資格を持つため、アレルギーへの理解は期待できるが、公式にアレルギー対応を謳った記述は確認されていない。来店前に電話（070-2352-3200）での事前確認を推奨。
オーナーは管理栄養士の資格保持者で、健康を意識した季節野菜中心のおばんざいを提供しており、野菜メニューの種類が多い。

name: おだしとワインとお料理と。motto (Odashi to Wine to Oryouri to. Motto)

claims.text: No kitchen gluten protocols or dedicated preparation areas are documented in any source. The menu includes fried items (shrimp fritters, fried wontons) alongside non-fried dishes, suggesting shared frying or preparation areas are likely.
Shoyu (soy sauce) versions of the ebisoba and likely the oden broth base will contain wheat. Standard Japanese soy sauce (shoyu) contains wheat unless specifically labeled tamari or GF.
Shrimp broth, bonito dashi, chashu pork, ham, and beef dishes are core to the menu; plant-based cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable in this kitchen.

No allergy handling procedures, allergen menus, or staff training documentation appear on any source. Phone reservations are accepted, which provides an opportunity to discuss dietary needs before visiting: 079-263-7388.
The restaurant is entirely non-smoking, which reduces one environmental irritant for sensitive diners.

name: おでん処 能古 (Oden-dokoro Noko)

claims.text: No information on cross-contamination controls is available. The kitchen handles fish cakes and processed items that routinely contain wheat starch, and the shared oden pot means any wheat-bearing ingredient contaminates the broth for all diners.

The house ginger soy sauce is described as conventional Japanese shoyu blended with cooking sake and oden broth. Standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat. No tamari or gluten-free shoyu option is mentioned.
The shared oden pot contains bonito-based dashi throughout, as well as fish cakes, beef tendon, and seafood. There is no plant-only broth or separate cooking vessel noted.

No allergy-handling procedures or allergen menu are mentioned on any source reviewed. Diners with celiac disease or severe allergies should contact the restaurant directly before visiting (tel: 079-284-7345).

Dashi base is kelp and bonito — no hidden soy sauce in the broth itself. Individual pieces can in principle be chosen to avoid certain proteins (e.g., opting for daikon, konnyaku, or tofu pieces) if wheat in the dipping sauce is the only concern.

name: おでん いち佳 (Oden Ichika)

claims.text: All-in-one communal oden pot with no separation between ingredients; wheat-containing items such as tsumire (which may contain binders) and soy-sauce-marinated components share the same broth.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is used both in the oden broth and in the Himeji-style ginger soy sauce condiment served at the table.
The house condiment 'karazou' (唐三) is described as a fermented chili-soy paste, meaning it also contains wheat via soy sauce.
Bonito-based dashi is the foundation of the oden broth; fish-paste tsumire and other animal-derived ingredients share the pot with any vegetable items.
No allergy or dietary accommodation information was found in any source. The restaurant operates as a solo-run counter with no documented awareness of gluten or vegan requirements.

name: おでんと串カツ姫路のお店 (Oden to Kushikatsu Himeji no Omise)

claims.text: Kushikatsu (deep-fried battered skewers) is one of the two core menu categories. Wheat batter is in heavy use throughout service. No dedicated gluten-free fryer is mentioned anywhere.
The ginger soy sauce condiment (生姜醤油) served with oden is standard Japanese shoyu, which contains wheat. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.
The oden broth is made from konbu and katsuo (bonito fish) dashi. All oden ingredients simmer in this shared broth, making plant-based isolation impossible even for nominally vegetable items.

No allergy handling protocols, allergen menus, or dietary accommodation procedures are published on any platform. The restaurant's own site, Tabelog, HotPepper, Gurunavi, and Hitosara all lack allergen information.
